subject: Oakridge: NQv2 rollout — p99 latency & error spike, emergency playbook
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@oakridgef.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@oakridgef.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in latency and errors after NQv2 rollout

Hi Kimberly,

We pushed your suggested model variant (NQv2, int8-fast qprofile) to production for a subset of traffic this morning and started seeing a large regression within ~30 minutes. Symptoms: p99 latency jumped from ~240ms to ~680ms, error rate (503s/timeout) increased to ~2.1% on /generate, and throughput dropped on our hot endpoints. We've attached our observability snapshot (p99 report) and included a short trace in the attachment.

What I gave to our SREs: they say GPU queues show decode stalls and a lot of retries against the same session IDs. This is hitting our checkout flow and causing visible drop-off for users. Can Redwood revert or route our traffic back to the previous model variant immediately? We need an ETA and an action plan.

Attachments: oakridge_p99_report_Aug24.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Sara
Director of Platform, Oakridge Financial

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Oakridge NQv2 rollout latency — immediate technical and commercial ask

Team — internal only. Oakridge reported production p99 jump and a throughput collapse after NQv2 went live to a ~25% canary. Key points below from initial traces:

- Impact: p99 x3, error-rate ~2% (customer measured), checkout path affected.
- Scope: Oakridge production, canary traffic ~25%, persistent after 30m.
- Customer reaction: High-impact, wants immediate rollback or routing to v1. They are asking for credits if this is an SLA breach.

Proposed immediate actions (urgent):
1) Technical: Rollback routing for Oakridge to v1 (full traffic) — low-risk, quick.
2) Infra: Provision additional instances on EU-west-us-1 for 2 hours if rollback causes transient load.
3) Engineering: Triage NQv2 qprofile (int8-fast) for KV cache behavior + decoder stalls, capture perf trace.
4) Comms: Kimberly/Marissa to lead customer update and offer provisional SLA credit pending RCA.

I've attached our suggested rollback playbook and flagged this for exec awareness. Jordan/Marcus — please confirm feasibility of immediate routing change and whether we need a hotfix.

Attachments: redwood_playbook_oakridge_rollback.md

— Kimberly
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Oakridge NQv2 rollout latency — technical readout

Quick tech readout after 3h of traces and perf samples:

- Root cause hypothesis: The int8-fast quantization profile in NQv2 changes KV cache layout and increases certain decode kernel loads, which in turn increases GPU scheduling contention for long-session requests. We are seeing repeated cache warmups causing stalls and a spike in dispatcher retries.
- Evidence: perf_trace_0824.json (attached) shows a chain of decoder stalls right before the 503s. CPU queuing was low; GPU CUDA kernel wait events rose sharply.

Immediate ask: approve immediate routing rollback + short term scale-up of Redwood Dedicated pool for Oakridge to absorb the transient while rollback completes. Also recommend disabling NQv2 qprofile by default until a controlled staging pass.

If granted, we'll: (1) flip routing today; (2) run an internal A/B replay in staging to isolate the KV/cache interaction; (3) prepare a targeted patch to KV cache allocation in NQv2.

— Jordan
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
[attachment: perf_trace_0824.json]
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@oakridgef.com>, ops@oakridgef.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary & proposed remediation (Oakridge NQv2)

Sara — following the bridge and internal triage: thank you for your patience. Executive summary below and proposed remediation steps.

Summary:
- What happened: A canary deployment of NQv2 (int8-fast qprofile) introduced a KV cache layout behavior that led to decode kernel contention and retry storms on long sessions, increasing p99 and transient 503s.
- Impact: We observed a ~3x p99 increase and ~2% error rate for the affected endpoints while NQv2 was active.

What we will do now (agreed plan):
1) Immediate: Rollback Oakridge traffic to the prior model variant (v1) — actioned now. Expect p99 to return to baseline within 15–30 minutes after routing stabilizes.
2) Capacity: Temporarily increase Dedicated capacity window for Oakridge for 2 hours to cover any transient spikes.
3) RCA: Engineering to run controlled A/B replay and validate KV cache fix. Target: patch and staging validation within 72 hours.
4) Commercial: We will issue a provisional SLA credit for the affected window and follow up with final credit after RCA.

Call to action for Oakridge: please confirm when you see p99 stabilize so we can close the incident.

Links: https://redwood.app/console/playbooks/oakridge-nqv2-rollback

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@oakridgef.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@oakridgef.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive summary & proposed remediation (Oakridge NQv2)

Team — quick update from Oakridge: after your rollback this morning traffic returned to expected latencies (p99 ~250ms) within ~12 minutes. Error rate dropped to baseline. Thank you for the fast response and the temporary capacity help.

We accept the provisional SLA credit and look forward to the RCA and plan to re-evaluate NQv2 in staging once the KV/cache behavior is resolved. Please keep us updated on the targeted patch timeline.

Sara Nguyen
Director of Platform, Oakridge Financial
